description: Claim verification with bound source citations. Takes a claim, retrieves evidence from eleven free sources, binds every citation to the exact text it cites, and reports whether the evidence contradicts the claim, agrees with it, or says nothing about it. Every response is a JSON object. All inputs arrive in the body. A contradiction is provable, not probable: it needs the same attribute with a different value AND that the citation is about the same subject as the claim. Absence of contradiction is never treated as truth.

rpc_types.notes: Every response is a JSON object. All inputs arrive in the body. No path params, no query params, no auth. Verdicts are CONTRADICTED, SUPPORTED, UNRESOLVED or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. UNRESOLVED is the default. A model assessment, when requested, is carried separately and cannot alter the verdict.

serving.backend: A small Node.js HTTP service with no dependencies beyond the runtime. Retrieval and reasoning are synchronous within the request.
serving.notes: Outbound calls go to en.wikipedia.org, www.wikidata.org, api.crossref.org, efts.sec.gov, export.arxiv.org, api.worldbank.org, www.ebi.ac.uk, api.openalex.org, openlibrary.org, musicbrainz.org and earthquake.usgs.gov. All free, none needing a key. Citations are bound to verbatim text, never to a summary. Missing data is reported missing and never filled in, interpolated, back-filled or coerced to zero.
